description: A Codex API key without alpha-search does not serve search: no account is eligible and the client gets an error.

headers.Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type, X-Api-Key, X-Goog-Api-Key, Anthropic-Version, Anthropic-Beta
headers.Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS
headers.Access-Control-Expose-Headers: X-CPA-TRACE-ID, X-CPA-VERSION, X-CPA-COMMIT, X-CPA-BUILD-DATE, X-CPA-SUPPORT-PLUGIN, X-CPA-HOME-VERSION, X-CPA-HOME-BUILD-DATE, X-SERVER-VERSION, X-SERVER-BUILD-DATE, Location, Retry-After, ETag, X-Request-Id, OpenAI-Request-Id

exceptions.reason: No account is eligible: an API key without alpha_search answers the call unsupported, and the new core answers that with 400 as for any endpoint no account serves; today's core answers 503. Whether a request no account can serve should answer 503 is not decided.

want.message: this API key does not serve Alpha Search (the account's alpha_search setting is off)

exceptions.reason: Today's core answers {"error": "<text>"} (auth_not_found: no auth available); the new core answers with an OpenAI-style error object that names why the key does not serve search.
The new core answers application/json; today's core's gin handler adds a charset to the error it writes itself.
Today's core sends a trace ID only once it has chosen an account; the new core sends one with every routed reply, including one where no account served the request.
